Landscape plan shows planting zones and identifies areas for parking lot landscaping (H.4) and street yard plantings (H.2, H.3) but does not provide specific dimensions (size and height) for individual proposed planters.

findings.comment: Scale verification completed for plan sheets (1" = 20') and location map (1" = 400'), but utility plan-profile sheets (19-20) and standard details sheets (23-28) were not examined visually to confirm scale legibility and format on all sheets.

Existing and proposed land uses are not shown on the cover sheet. The cover sheet identifies the project as 'Valley View Townhomes' and indicates R3 occupancy classification, but does not provide a summary listing existing conditions versus proposed multi-family residential use.

Adjoining land uses not labeled on site plan or location map. The single sheet attempts to display the site plan drawing with all buildings, utilities, and infrastructure along with five data tables, eight text note blocks, benchmark data, and detailed lighting figures, resulting in highly dense visual presentation with minimal white space. Information should be distributed across multiple sheets to ensure clarity and legibility at the required scale.

Location map exists on cover sheet with north arrow, but visual clarity and whether site location is sufficiently clear relative to surrounding context could not be fully verified without examining the source document.

findings.comment: Sheet 4 is labeled 'Existing Conditions Survey' and the guide indicates it shows existing topography and existing conditions. However, visual verification that the sheet reflects current (not proposed) grades and layout, and whether it is clearly distinguished from the demolition plan, requires examination of the actual source document.

Existing Conditions Sheet (Sheet 4) does not clearly identify and label which improvements from prior site plans will remain and which will be demolished. The prior site plan (SP-97-0145CS) included a nursing care facility demolished in June 2022; however, Sheet 4 does not explicitly label 'To Remain' or 'Will be Demolished' for any improvements from prior site plans. This information must be clearly documented on the Existing Conditions Sheet or Demolition Plan with explicit labeling.

Property boundary lines are shown on site plan, grading plan, ESC plan, utility plan, and addressing plan, but are absent from the landscape plan. Property boundaries must appear on all applicable civil plan sheets per UCM 2.5.1.E.9.

Property boundary bearings show inconsistencies across sheets: Sheet 9 shows N62°36'57"W, Sheet 8 shows N63°39'57"W, and Sheet 29 shows N63°36'57"W for nominally the same boundary segment. Verify that all property boundary dimensions and bearings match the recorded Mecey Subdivision plat (Vol. 73, Pg. 76) and resolve discrepancies with clarification notes or a revised survey.

Property boundary linetype is inconsistent across plan sheets. Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts the property boundary as a heavy dash-dot line, while Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) depicts it as a solid line. Property boundary linework must use consistent symbology throughout all discipline sheets.

Building use or function (Multi-Family Residential) is not labeled directly on building footprints on the site plan. Use information appears only in data tables on the plan sheet, not as direct labels on structures. Per BCM 1.2.7, site plan must show building location and size with use identification.

Existing versus proposed status is not labeled consistently. Existing adjacent buildings are labeled "Existing Apartment Building," but proposed buildings (Bldg. 1-8) are not labeled "Proposed" - only identified by building numbers. UCM 2.5.1.E.11 requires consistent labeling of existing versus proposed improvements.

Unit types (Two-Bedroom and Three-Bedroom) are not labeled on the site plan for multi-family residential buildings. Only unit numbers (Unit 101-806) are shown; unit types are not identified on the plans. Per City of Austin Addressing Standards, unit types must be labeled on site plan for multi-family residential projects.

Widths of vehicular access points are not shown in the Site Data Table. Although access point widths are depicted on the site plan drawing (22.5' for Type II driveway and 26.0' for Type III driveway), these dimensions must be included in the SDT for comprehensive site data documentation.

Open space areas are required to be delineated on the site plan sheet. Visual delineation of specific open space areas cannot be confirmed from the submitted document analysis without explicit identification on the drawing.

Building height measurement methodology cannot be verified. LDC § 25-1-21(50) requires height to be measured from the average of the highest and lowest grades adjacent to each building. The site plan shows building heights and benchmarks but does not show the grade baseline calculation (average of highest and lowest adjacent grades) for any building. The grading plan must clearly indicate how the height baseline was established for each building to confirm compliance.
applicableAreas: Building height calculations and grading plan

findings.comment: Building height calculation baseline cannot be verified. The grading plan and elevation sheets do not explicitly show the grade baseline calculation methodology (average of highest and lowest adjacent grades) used for height measurements. LDC § 25-1-21(50) requires this methodology. Provide detailed grading and elevation sheets showing clearly marked grade reference points and demonstrating that height is measured from the average of the highest and lowest adjacent grades, not from the lowest grade only.
applicableAreas: Grading plan and building elevation sheets

findings.comment: Multi-story buildings (Buildings 1-8) lack a floor-by-floor area breakdown table. The Building Data Table shows only total GFA per building without identifying square footage allocated to each floor level. Provide a floor-by-floor GFA breakdown for each building to verify that all enclosed areas with clear height exceeding 6 feet are properly included and that parking or other excluded areas are correctly omitted from the total GFA.
applicableAreas: all eight buildings (4-plex, 5-plex, and 6-plex configurations with up to 3 stories)

findings.comment: FAR is not expressed as a ratio in X:1 format on any site plan sheet. FAR is not shown on the cover sheet or the site plan (Sheet 9). Applicant must calculate and display FAR as a ratio (GFA ÷ Gross Site Area = approximately 0.891:1 for this project) on the site data table.

Bedroom count per unit type cannot be verified from the available site plan documentation. Unit type details must be shown in floor plans or a detailed building schedule.

Total bedroom count for the entire development is not explicitly documented. While the count can be calculated from unit breakdown (16 two-bedroom units + 23 three-bedroom units = 101 total bedrooms), it must be directly stated in the site plan documentation for clarity. Parking requirement calculations in Appendix A reference bedroom count, making this a critical data point.
applicableAreas: Building Data Table on Site Plan

findings.comment: Building heights are shown in feet on the site plan data table (Sheet 9), but elevation sheets—which are the primary location for detailed height labeling—are not provided. Provide building elevation sheets with heights clearly labeled in feet from the average adjacent grade to the applicable roof point.

Building height is not labeled in number of stories on elevation sheets. While Sheet 9 notes 'Maximum Number of Building Stories = 3,' individual story counts are not labeled for each of the 8 buildings. Provide elevation sheets labeling the number of stories for each building.

Heights of individual buildings are shown in the Site Plan data table (Sheet 9) ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1", with maximum height of 36'-1" (Building 3) identified, but no elevation sheets are provided where heights would be clearly separated by building. Provide architectural elevation sheets showing heights for each individual building.

Building height values show discrepancies across plan documents. The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values (e.g., Building 1: 686.25, Building 2: 684.50) that differ from the Finished Floor Elevations shown on Sheet 11 Grading Plan and Sheet 29 Addressing Plan (e.g., Building 1: FFE 687.50, Building 2: FFE 685.50). The difference between 'Average (MSL)' and FFE is not explained, creating confusion about which value represents the grade baseline for height measurement. Ensure all height values are consistent across elevation sheets, site plan data tables, grading plan, addressing plan, and project narrative, and reconcile any differences with clear notation of whether values represent AAG, FFE, or finished grade at specific locations.

Compatibility height limit compliance cannot be verified. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061 (MF-2 zoning within 75 feet of SF-3 triggering property). The applicable limits are: 40 feet maximum within 50 feet of triggering property; 60 feet maximum between 50–75 feet. However, the site plan does not show distance zone boundaries, does not identify the adjacent SF-3 property line, and does not document building locations relative to the triggering property. Distance zone notation and cross-sectional documentation are required to verify compliance.
applicableAreas: all eight buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

findings.comment: Compatibility distance zone boundaries are not shown on the site plan or elevation drawings. The site is subject to Article 10 compatibility standards per LDC § 25-2-1061. Elevation drawings must show the 50-foot and 75-foot distance zone boundary lines from the SF-3 triggering property and dashed reference lines at the applicable maximum permitted heights (40 feet within the 50-foot zone; 60 feet in the 50–75-foot zone) to graphically demonstrate compliance.
applicableAreas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

findings.comment: Cross-sectional elevation views are not provided. A cross-section is required showing the building profile relative to the SF-3 triggering property line, with distance zone boundaries (50-foot and 75-foot) clearly labeled, proposed building heights in each zone, and maximum allowed heights for each zone, all drawn to scale with dimensions labeled. This graphical representation is necessary to verify compliance with Article 10 compatibility height limits per LDC § 25-2-1061.
applicableAreas: all buildings relative to SF-3 triggering property

findings.comment: Rooftop structures above the maximum permitted building height are not labeled on elevation sheets as height limit exceptions. Without architectural elevation drawings, the presence of rooftop structures (parapets, mechanical equipment, chimneys, vents, stairways, elevator penthouses, etc.) and their relationship to the height limit line cannot be verified. Elevation sheets must clearly show and label any rooftop elements that extend above the maximum permitted building height.

Rooftop structure height exceptions cannot be verified without elevation sheets showing the height limit line and any overage calculations. The maximum allowable overage per § 25-2-531 is the greater of: (1) 15% of permitted height; (2) federal/state compliance amount; (3) engineering standard for stacks/vents; or (4) 30% for spires. Elevation sheets must provide a calculation demonstrating that any rooftop extensions remain within the allowable overage, with the calculation shown on the drawing.

For buildings subject to upper-story step-back requirements, the step-back location and dimensions are not shown on elevation sheets with required dimension callouts. The site plan does not document whether step-back requirements apply to these buildings. Elevation sheets must clearly show step-back locations, dimensions, and setback measurements if required by applicable zoning standards.

Fences and retaining walls are shown on the site plan along the property perimeter (wood fence and concrete retaining walls noted on Sheets 9 and 31), but because required zoning setback lines are not drawn on the plans, the relationship between fence locations and building setback lines cannot be verified. Additionally, fence heights are not labeled.
applicableAreas: property perimeter fences and retaining walls

findings.comment: Article 10 compatibility standards applicability has been incorrectly determined. The site is zoned MF-2, which is less restrictive than MF-4, and is located adjacent to an SF-3-zoned property. SF-3 is SF-5 or more restrictive and qualifies as a triggering property under § 25-2-1053. If the development is within 75 feet of this SF-3 property boundary, Article 10 compatibility standards apply. The applicant marked 'No' on the consolidated application for compatibility standards applicability, but this appears to be incorrect. Clarify whether the southern boundary is within 75 feet of the triggering property, and if so, prepare a compatibility analysis and revised plans demonstrating Article 10 compliance.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to SF-3 zoning

findings.comment: If Article 10 compatibility is triggered (site within 75 ft of SF-3 triggering property), the required compatibility buffer is not shown at the correct width along the shared property line. The compatibility buffer must be 25 feet wide (or 15 feet if the development site is less than 75 feet wide measured from the shared triggering property line), shown as a landscaped zone complying with § 25-8-700 planting requirements, and extending along the full length of the property line shared with the triggering property. No such labeled and dimensioned buffer line appears on the site plan or landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to SF-3 property

findings.comment: Triggering property or properties are not clearly identified on the site plan compatibility sheets with all required information. While the site plan vision analysis identified adjacent zoning labels (SF-3 on south), there is no separate compatibility exhibit clearly labeling the triggering property with its zoning designation (SF-3) and dwelling unit count (required to confirm it qualifies as a triggering property under § 25-2-1053). Prepare a compatibility exhibit showing the triggering property location, zoning, and dwelling unit count, and clearly label it on all relevant plan sheets.

Separate compatibility exhibit is not provided or is incomplete. If Article 10 compatibility is triggered, the required standalone compatibility exhibit must show: property boundaries, on-site and off-site zoning boundaries (including all triggering properties and applicable combining districts), distances from triggering property boundary to existing and proposed structures, distances to surface improvements (parking, driveways, drainage features), and location of existing structures on triggering properties. This documentation is required to demonstrate compliance with § 25-2-1061 (height limits), § 25-2-1062 (buffer), and § 25-2-1063 (screening).

Fence height compliance cannot be verified. Wood fences and concrete retaining walls are depicted on the site plan sheets, but no heights are labeled on any sheet. Construction type and design details are insufficient to verify compliance.
applicableAreas: wooden privacy fences shown on site plan

Dumpster or permanently placed refuse receptacle location not identified on site plan to verify 20-foot setback from properties zoned or used as SF-5 or more restrictive (LA, RR, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, SF-4A, SF-4B, SF-5). Zoning district boundary not shown or labeled for all adjacent zones. The site abuts MF-2, MF-4-CO, MF-2-CO, and SF-3 zoning districts. While north (MF-4-CO) and east (MF-2-CO) are labeled, the SF-3 zone boundary to the south is not shown or labeled.

findings.comment: Zoning designations on mylars cannot be verified. Mylar documents are not available in the submitted project files; review of mylar compliance with zoning designation requirements cannot be completed without access to these documents.

Verification of building dimension callouts on site plan cannot be completed. Exterior lighting above the second floor restriction not explicitly stated on site plan. This restriction must be explicitly documented.

findings.comment: Mechanical equipment noise specifications not found in submitted documentation. Three conflicting open space area figures exist: Site Data Table shows 4,710 SF provided (vs. 4,709.62 SF required), Site Plan drawing shows 4,960 SF, and Landscape Calculations show 5,859 SF provided (vs. 4,715 SF required based on 94,293 SF site area). Site area basis varies across documents: Sheet 9 uses 94,192 SF; Sheet 35 uses 94,293 SF. This 101 SF difference affects required open space amounts (4,709.62 SF vs. 4,715 SF). Verify controlling site area against legal description and survey; if 94,293 SF is correct, recalculate requirements accordingly.

Open space area not labeled with type. Site plan shows only 'Common Open Space 4,960 sf' without specifying which of the 11 permitted types applies (landscaped area, plaza, play area, etc.). Revise label to include specific open space type per LDC § 2.7.3.A.

Open space not shown as a percentage of the applicable site area in site data table. Sheet 9 Site Data Table shows 'Common Open Space provided: 4710' in square feet only, with no percentage calculation shown. Cannot verify open space location outside required street yard. Provide clear boundary delineation.
